front.title: Guidelines on the Cryptographic Algorithms to Accompany the Usage of Standards GOST R 34.10-2012 and GOST R 34.11-2012

abstract.t: The purpose of this document is to make the specifications of the cryptographic algorithms defined by the Russian national standards GOST R 34.10-2012 and GOST R 34.11-2012 available to the Internet community for their implementation in the cryptographic protocols based on the accompanying algorithms.

These specifications define the pseudorandom functions, the key agreement algorithm based on the Diffie-Hellman algorithm and a hash function, the parameters of elliptic curves, the key derivation functions, and the key export functions.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The accompanying algorithms are intended for the implementation of cryptographic protocols. This memo contains a description of the accompanying algorithms based on the Russian national standards GOST R 34.10-2012 and GOST R 34.11-2012 . The English versions of these standards can be found in and ; the English version of the encryption standard GOST 28147-89 (which is used in the key export functions) can be found in .
The specifications of algorithms and parameters proposed in this memo are provided on the basis of experience in the development of the cryptographic protocols, as described in , , and .

This memo describes the pseudorandom functions, the key agreement algorithm based on the Diffie-Hellman algorithm and a hash function, the parameters of elliptic curves, the key derivation functions, and the key export functions necessary to ensure interoperability of security protocols that make use of the Russian cryptographic standards GOST R 34.10-2012 digital signature algorithm and GOST R 34.11-2012 cryptographic hash function.

section.name: Basic Terms, Definitions, and Notations
section.t: This document uses the following terms and definitions for the sets and operations on the elements of these sets:

dl.dd: Exclusive-or of two binary vectors of the same length.

The finite vector space over GF(2) of dimension n, n >= 0, with the (xor) operation. For n = 0, the V_0 space consists of a single empty element of size 0. If U is an element of V_n, then U = (u_(n-1), u_(n-2), ..., u_1, u_0), where u_i in {0, 1}.

The set of byte vectors of size r, r >= 0, for r = 0 the V_(8, r) set consists of a single empty element of size 0. If W is an element of V_(8, r), r > 0, then W = (w^0, w^1, ..., w^(r-1)), where w^0, w^1, ..., w^(r-1) are elements of V_8.

The bit representation of the element W = (w^0, w^1, ..., w^(r-1)) of V_(8, r) is an element (w_(8r-1), w_(8r-2), ..., w_1, w_0) of V_(8*r), where w^0 = (w_7, w_6, ..., w_0), w^1 = (w_15, w_14, ..., w_8), ..., w^(r-1) = (w_(8r-1), w_(8r-2), ..., w_(8r-8)) are elements of V_8.

If n is a multiple of 8, r = n/8, then the byte representation of the element W = (w_(n-1), w_(n-2), ..., w_0) of V_n is a byte vector (w^0, w^1, ..., w^(r-1)) of V_(8, r), where w^0 = (w_7, w_6, ..., w_0), w^1 = (w_15, w_14, ..., w_8), ..., w^(r-1) = (w_(8r-1), w_(8r-2), ..., w_(8r-8)) are elements of V_8.

Concatenation of byte vectors A and B, i.e., if A in V_(8, r1), B in V_(8, r2), A = (a^0, a^1, ..., a^(r1-1)) and B = (b^0, b^1, ..., b^(r2-1)), then A|B = (a^0, a^1, ..., a^(r1-1), b^0, b^1, ..., b^(r2-1)) is an element of V_(8, r1+r2).
An arbitrary element of V_n. If K in V_n, then its size (in bits) is equal to n, where n can be an arbitrary natural number.

section.t: To generate a byte sequence of the size r with functions that give a longer output, the output is truncated to the first r bytes. This remark applies to the following functions:
Hereinafter, all data are provided in byte representation unless otherwise specified.

If a function is defined outside this document (e.g., H_256) and its definition requires arguments in bit representation, it is assumed that the bit representations of the arguments are formed immediately before the calculation of the function (in particular, immediately after the application of the operation (|) to the byte representation of the arguments).

If the output of another function defined outside of this document is used as an argument of the functions defined below and it has the bit representation, then it is assumed that an output MUST have a length that is a multiple of 8 and that it will be translated into the byte representation in advance.

When a point on an elliptic curve is given to an input of a hash function, affine coordinates for short Weierstrass form are used (see ): an x coordinate value is fed first, a y coordinate value is fed second, both in little-endian format.

section.name: HMAC Functions
section.t: This section defines the HMAC transformations based on the GOST R 34.11-2012 algorithm.

section.name: HMAC_GOSTR3411_2012_256
section.t: This HMAC transformation is based on the GOST R 34.11-2012 hash function with 256-bit output. The object identifier of this transformation is shown below:
section.artwork: id-tc26-hmac-gost-3411-12-256::= {iso(1) member-body(2) ru(643) rosstandart(7) tc26(1) algorithms(1) mac(4) hmac-gost- 3411-12-256(1)}.
section.t: This algorithm uses H_256 as a hash function for HMAC, described in . The method of forming the values of ipad and opad is also specified in . The size of HMAC_GOSTR3411_2012_256 output is equal to 32 bytes, the block size of the iterative procedure for the H_256 compression function is equal to 64 bytes (in the notation of , L = 32 and B = 64, respectively).

section.name: Pseudorandom Functions
section.t: This section defines four HMAC-based PRF transformations recommended for usage. Two of them are designed for the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol and two are designed for the IPsec protocol.

section.name: PRF_TLS_GOSTR3411_2012_256
section.t: This is the transformation providing the pseudorandom function for the TLS protocol (1.0 and higher versions) in accordance with GOST R 34.11-2012 . It uses the P_GOSTR3411_2012_256 function that is similar to the P_hash function defined in , where the HMAC_GOSTR3411_2012_256 function (defined in of this document) is used as the HMAC_hash function.
section.artwork: PRF_TLS_GOSTR3411_2012_256 (secret, label, seed) = = P_GOSTR3411_2012_256 (secret, label | seed).
section.t: Label and seed values MUST be assigned by a protocol, their lengths SHOULD be fixed by a protocol in order to avoid possible collisions.

section.name: PRF_TLS_GOSTR3411_2012_512
section.t: This is the transformation providing the pseudorandom function for the TLS protocol (1.0 and higher versions) in accordance with GOST R 34.11-2012 . It uses the P_GOSTR3411_2012_512 function that is similar to the P_hash function defined in , where the HMAC_GOSTR3411_2012_512 function (defined in of this document) is used as the HMAC_hash function.
section.artwork: PRF_TLS_GOSTR3411_2012_512 (secret, label, seed) = = P_GOSTR3411_2012_512 (secret, label | seed).
section.t: Label and seed values MUST be assigned by a protocol, their lengths SHOULD be fixed by a protocol in order to avoid possible collisions.

section.name: PRFs for the IKEv2 Protocol Based on GOST R 34.11-2012
section.t: The specification for the Internet Key Exchange protocol version 2 (IKEv2) defines the usage of PRFs in various parts of the protocol for the purposes of generating and authenticating keying material.

IKEv2 has no default PRF. This document specifies that HMAC_GOSTR3411_2012_256 may be used as the "prf" function in the "prf+" function for the IKEv2 protocol (PRF_IPSEC_PRFPLUS_GOSTR3411_2012_256). Also, this document specifies that HMAC_GOSTR3411_2012_512 may be used as the "prf" function in the "prf+" function for the IKEv2 protocol (PRF_IPSEC_PRFPLUS_GOSTR3411_2012_512).

section.name: VKO Algorithms for Key Agreement
section.t: This section specifies the key agreement algorithms based on GOST R 34.10-2012 .

section.name: VKO_GOSTR3410_2012_256
section.t: The VKO_GOSTR3410_2012_256 transformation is used for agreement of 256-bit keys and is based on the 256-bit version of GOST R 34.11-2012 . This algorithm can be applied for a key agreement using GOST R 34.10-2012 with 256-bit or 512-bit private keys.

The algorithm is designed to produce an encryption key or a keying material of size 256 bits to be used in various cryptographic protocols. A key or a keying material KEK_VKO (x, y, UKM) is produced from the private key x of one side, the public key y*P of the opposite side and the User Keying Material (UKM) value.
The algorithm can be used for static and ephemeral keys with the public key size n >= 512 bits including the case where one side uses a static key and the other uses an ephemeral one.

The UKM parameter is optional (the default UKM = 1) and can take any integer value from 1 to 2^(n/2)-1. It is allowed to use a non-zero UKM of an arbitrary size that does not exceed n/2 bits. If at least one of the parties uses static keys, the RECOMMENDED length of UKM is 64 bits or more.
KEK_VKO (x, y, UKM) is calculated using the formulas:
section.artwork: KEK_VKO (x, y, UKM) = H_256 (K (x, y, UKM)),
section.t: where m and q are the parameters of an elliptic curve defined in the GOST R 34.10-2012 standard (m is an elliptic curve points group order, q is an order of a cyclic subgroup), P is a non-zero point of the subgroup; P is defined by a protocol.

This algorithm is defined similar to the one specified in , but applies the hash function H_256 instead of the hash function GOST R 34.11-94 (referred to as "gostR3411"). In addition, K(x, y, UKM) is calculated with public key size n >= 512 bits and UKM has a size up to n/2 bits.

section.name: VKO_GOSTR3410_2012_512
section.t: The VKO_GOSTR3410_2012_512 transformation is used for agreement of 512-bit keys and is based on the 512-bit version of GOST R 34.11-2012 . This algorithm can be applied for a key agreement using GOST R 34.10-2012 with 512-bit private keys.

The algorithm is designed to produce an encryption key or a keying material of size 512 bits to be used in various cryptographic protocols. A key or a keying material KEK_VKO (x, y, UKM) is produced from the private key x of one side, the public key y*P of the opposite side and the UKM value, considered as an integer.
The algorithm can be used for static and ephemeral keys with the public key size n >= 1024 bits including the case where one side uses a static key and the other uses an ephemeral one.

The UKM parameter is optional (the default UKM = 1) and can take any integer value from 1 to 2^(n/2)-1. It is allowed to use a non-zero UKM of an arbitrary size that does not exceed n/2 bits. If at least one of the parties uses static keys, the RECOMMENDED length of UKM is 128 bits or more.
KEK_VKO (x, y, UKM) is calculated using the formulas:
section.artwork: KEK_VKO (x, y, UKM) = H_512 (K (x, y, UKM)),
section.t: where m and q are the parameters of an elliptic curve defined in the GOST R 34.10-2012 standard (m is an elliptic curve points group order, q is an order of a cyclic subgroup), P is a non-zero point of the subgroup; P is defined by a protocol.

This algorithm is defined similar to the one specified in , but applies the hash function H_512 instead of the hash function GOST R 34.11-94 (referred to as "gostR3411"). In addition, K(x, y, UKM) is calculated with public key size n >= 1024 bits and UKM has a size up to n/2 bits.

section.name: The Key Derivation Function KDF_TREE_GOSTR3411_2012_256
section.t: The key derivation function KDF_TREE_GOSTR3411_2012_256 based on the HMAC_GOSTR3411_2012_256 function is given by:
section.artwork: KDF_TREE_GOSTR3411_2012_256 (K_in, label, seed, R) = K(1) | K(2) | K(3) | K(4) |...,
section.t: where:

dl.dd: Derivation key.
The parameters that MUST be assigned by a protocol; their lengths SHOULD be fixed by a protocol.
A fixed external parameter, with possible values of 1, 2, 3, or 4.
Iteration counter.
Byte representation of the iteration counter (in the network byte order); the number of bytes in the representation [i]_b is equal to R (no more than 4 bytes).
The required size (in bits) of the generated keying material (an integer, not exceeding 256*(2^(8*R)-1)).
Byte representation of L, in network byte order (variable length: no leading zero bytes added).

section.t: The key derivation function KDF_TREE_GOSTR3411_2012_256 is intended for generating a keying material of size L, not exceeding 256*(2^(8*R)-1) bits, and utilizing general principles of the input and output for the key derivation function outlined in Section 5.1 of NIST SP 800-108 . The HMAC_GOSTR3411_2012_256 algorithm described in is selected as a pseudorandom function.

Each key derived from the keying material formed using the derivation key K_in (0-level key) may be a 1-level derivation key and may be used to generate a new keying material. The keying material derived from the first level derivation key can be split down into the second level derivation keys. The application of this procedure leads to the construction of the key tree with the root key and the formation of the keying material to the hierarchy of the levels, as described in Section 6 of NIST SP 800-108 . The partitioning procedure for keying material at each level is defined in accordance with a specific protocol.

section.name: The Key Derivation Function KDF_GOSTR3411_2012_256
section.t: The KDF_GOSTR3411_2012_256 function is equivalent to the function KDF_TREE_GOSTR3411_2012_256, when R = 1, L = 256, and is given by:
section.artwork: KDF_GOSTR3411_2012_256 (K_in, label, seed) = HMAC_GOSTR3411_2012_256 (K_in, 0x01 | label | 0x00 | seed | 0x01 | 0x00),
section.t: where:

dl.dd: Derivation key.
The parameters that MUST be assigned by a protocol; their lengths SHOULD be fixed by a protocol.

section.name: Key Wrap and Key Unwrap
section.t: Wrapped representation of a secret key K (256-bit GOST 28147-89 key, 256-bit or 512-bit GOST R 34.10-2012 private key) is formed as follows by using a given export key K_e (GOST 28147-89 key) and a random seed vector:

ol.li: Generate a random seed vector from 8 up to 16 bytes.

where the KDF_GOSTR3411_2012_256 function (see ) is used as a key derivation function for the fixed label value

ol.li: GOST 28147-89 Message Authentication Code (MAC) value (4-byte) for the data K and the key KEK_e (K_e, seed) is calculated; the initialization vector (IV) in this case is equal to the first 8 bytes of seed. The resulting value is denoted as CEK_MAC.
The key K is encrypted with the GOST 28147-89 algorithm in the Electronic Codebook (ECB) mode with the key KEK_e (K_e, seed). The result is denoted as CEK_ENC.
The wrapped representation of the key is (seed | CEK_ENC | CEK_MAC).

section.t: The value of key K is restored from the wrapped representation of the key and the export key K_e as follows:

ol.li: Obtain the seed, CEK_ENC and CEK_MAC values from the wrapped representation of the key.

where the KDF_GOSTR3411_2012_256 function (see ) is used as a key derivation function for the fixed label value

ol.li: The CEK_ENC field is decrypted with the GOST 28147-89 algorithm in the Electronic Codebook (ECB) mode with the key KEK_e(K_e, seed). The unwrapped key K is assumed to be equal to the result of decryption.

GOST 28147-89 MAC value (4-byte) for the data K and the key KEK_e(K_e, seed) is calculated; the initialization vector (IV) in this case is equal to the first 8 bytes of seed. If the result is not equal to CEK_MAC, an error is returned.

section.name: The Parameters of Elliptic Curves
section.t: This section defines the elliptic curves parameters and object identifiers that are RECOMMENDED for usage with the signature and verification algorithms of the digital signature in accordance with the GOST R 34.10-2012 standard and with the key agreement algorithms VKO_GOSTR3410_2012_256 and VKO_GOSTR3410_2012_512.
This document does not negate the use of other parameters of elliptic curves.
